question.problem: Consider the function $f:{R}^{3}\to R$ defined by $f(x)={x}^{T}x.$ What is the total derivative of $f$ with respect to $x?$
question.worked_solution:
The total derivative of a scalar-valued function $f:{R}^{n}\to R$ with respect to a vector $x\in {R}^{n}$ is the row vector

$$
\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x}=[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂f}{∂{x}_{2}} & ⋯ & \frac{∂f}{∂{x}_{n}}\end{aligned}]\in {R}^{1\times n}.
$$

In our case, the function 

- acts on a vector $x\in {R}^{3},$ and

- outputs a scalar $f({x}_{1},{x}_{2},{x}_{3})\in R$ defined by 

$$
f(x)={x}^{T}x=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & {x}_{2} & {x}_{3}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}]={x}_{1}^{2}+{x}_{2}^{2}+{x}_{3}^{2}.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x} & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂f}{∂{x}_{2}} & \frac{∂f}{∂{x}_{3}}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂}{∂{x}_{1}}({x}_{1}^{2}+{x}_{2}^{2}+{x}_{3}^{2}) & \frac{∂}{∂{x}_{2}}({x}_{1}^{2}+{x}_{2}^{2}+{x}_{3}^{2}) & \frac{∂}{∂{x}_{3}}({x}_{1}^{2}+{x}_{2}^{2}+{x}_{3}^{2})\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2{x}_{1} & 2{x}_{2} & 2{x}_{3}\end{aligned}]\in {R}^{1\times 3}.\end{aligned}
$$

We can also write this as

$$
\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x}=2{x}^{T}.
$$
